gap: No result ChatGPT got states an independent wall-socket measurement for the UGREEN DXP2800 (igor'sLAB: 5.6 W standby, 14.5 W during transfers with one NVMe, 33.2/35.6 dB(A) at 40 cm) set beside NAS Compares' 10 W idle / 21 W full-load figures for the Synology DS225+ and its observation that DSM alone uses 28–38% of the DS225+'s 2 GB RAM before any container is installed.
standout_why: Compared against homelabwise.com (DXP2800 16.38/5.24 W, DS225+ 16.98/6.08 W, all UGREEN/Synology ratings), nasdecoded.com (no measurements, generic 280 MB/s 2.5GbE estimate), bitdoze.com (unattributed 20–35 W estimate) and starryhope.com best-2-bay (one Notebookcheck figure, 14.84–20.14 W idle for the DXP2800 GT, and a Liliputing PCIe x1 note). None gives a named, independent power or noise measurement for the sub-$500 candidates themselves, none gives a measured RAM-headroom figure for the DS225+, and none gives measured SMB/iperf throughput for the F2-425 Plus. The DXP2800 and DS225+ numbers are new and bear directly on Docker suitability; they do not overturn the pick, so 2 rather than 3.
decides: Confirms the UGREEN DXP2800 as the pick: igor'sLAB measured 14.5 W at the wall while transferring and 5.6 W in standby with an NVMe-only setup, which is the configuration a Docker/Immich user would run before adding HDDs, and noise stayed at the 33.2 dB(A) room floor at idle. It argues against the Synology DS225+ for Immich: NAS Compares found DSM already consuming 28–38% of the 2 GB at idle, leaving roughly 1.2–1.4 GB for Immich's server, database and ML containers before an upgrade, and its measured 10 W idle / 21 W load is not enough of a power advantage to offset that. The Beelink ME mini (8 W idle, 15 W max CPU, measured by Michael Klements on TrueNAS) is the lowest-power option but has no SATA bays. The F2-425 Plus's 5GbE is real in iperf3 (4.71 Gbit/s per CNX Software) but two HDDs only wrote at 110 MB/s uncached, so the dual 5GbE does not help a two-HDD Immich library much. The DXP2800 GT measured by Notebookcheck is quieter (29.11 dB(A)) but at $509.99 is over budget.
